quests.instruction: Choose the topic sentence: the sentence that states the main idea of the paragraph.
quests.prompt: Read the paragraph: 'Evening classes suit adults who work during the day. They start after 6 p.m., when most jobs have finished. Many colleges also offer them at a low price. Some courses even run on Saturday mornings.'
options: Some courses even run on Saturday mornings.
Many colleges also offer them at a low price.
They start after 6 p.m., when most jobs have finished.
Evening classes suit adults who work during the day.
quests.hint: The main idea is the sentence the other sentences explain or support.
quests.explanation: The first sentence names the main idea. The other three give details about times, cost and extra options that support it.

quests.instruction: Choose the topic sentence. It does not have to come first.
quests.prompt: Read the paragraph: 'Volunteers sort donated clothes on Mondays. They deliver food parcels on Wednesdays. On Saturdays they help run the shop. Volunteering at the community centre keeps people busy all week.'
options: They deliver food parcels on Wednesdays.
Volunteering at the community centre keeps people busy all week.
On Saturdays they help run the shop.
Volunteers sort donated clothes on Mondays.
quests.hint: Which sentence covers all of the others together?
quests.explanation: The last sentence sums up the days described before it. Each of the other sentences names just one task on one day.

quests.instruction: Select the THREE sentences that are supporting details. One sentence is the main idea.
quests.prompt: Paragraph: a writer is discussing weekend markets.
options: Customers can talk to the person who made the product.
Small sellers can test new products without a big risk.
Weekend markets are helpful to small businesses.
Stallholders pay less than shop rent.
quests.hint: Find the sentence that the other three help to prove.
quests.explanation: The main idea is that markets help small businesses. Lower costs, direct contact and low-risk testing are supporting details for it.

quests.instruction: Choose the best topic sentence for these supporting details.
quests.prompt: Details: students can join clubs, meet new people, and try activities they have never done before.
options: Every school should have its own football team.
Clubs are usually held in classrooms and school halls.
After-school clubs give students chances to grow beyond lessons.
Some students go straight home when lessons end.
quests.hint: A topic sentence must cover all the details, not just one.
quests.explanation: The best sentence covers joining, meeting people and trying new things. The others mention clubs or students without covering what the details say.

quests.instruction: Choose the best opening sentence for the paragraph.
quests.prompt: Details: many gyms charge monthly fees; some add joining costs and charges for classes; together these can cost more than a yearly swimming pass.
options: Regular exercise is important for good health.
Some gyms stay open for twenty-four hours.
Gym membership can cost more than people expect.
Gyms have many different kinds of equipment.
quests.hint: Which sentence makes a point that all three details support?
quests.explanation: The details all explain extra costs, so the topic sentence must be about cost. The other options are true but about equipment, health and opening hours.

quests.instruction: Choose the topic sentence that fits.
quests.prompt: Details: employees can reply when it suits them; no one has to stop their work; messages stay in one place for later.
options: Written messages can work better than quick calls for routine updates.
Some managers dislike receiving long emails, especially when they arrive late in the day.
Calls are a common way to communicate at work, and many teams hold them at the start of the day.
Employees use many different apps for chatting, including some that the company has not approved.
quests.hint: The topic sentence should take a position that the details support.
quests.explanation: The details show benefits of written messages, so the best opening states that position. The alternatives describe communication in general.

quests.instruction: Choose the topic sentence that is neither too broad nor too narrow.
quests.prompt: Supporting details: the bins were clearly labelled, staff sorted paper and plastic, and waste fell by a third.
options: The environment is important to all of us.
The blue bin was placed beside the kitchen sink on Monday.
Clearly labelled bins helped our office reduce its waste.
Waste is a problem for every country in the world.
quests.hint: It should be big enough to cover the details but small enough to stay on the office.
quests.explanation: The right sentence covers labelling, sorting and lower waste in this office. Two options are too general and one is too specific to one bin.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that is TOO BROAD to open a paragraph.
quests.prompt: The paragraph will discuss a school's new lunch menu that adds two vegetarian meals a week.
options: Students voted for the changes in a recent survey.
The new lunch menu adds two vegetarian meals every week.
The menu will be updated at the start of each term.
Food matters to people everywhere.
quests.hint: A broad sentence could open a paragraph about almost anything.
quests.explanation: 'Food matters to people everywhere' says nothing about this menu. The other sentences are all about the school's new menu.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that is TOO NARROW to be a topic sentence.
quests.prompt: The paragraph will explain the benefits of walking to school: exercise, less traffic and time with friends.
options: Walking is one of the simplest ways to get around.
Walking to school gives students exercise and reduces traffic.
Travel is a big part of everyone's daily life.
Last Tuesday it took me eleven minutes to walk to school.
quests.hint: A topic sentence must be able to hold several supporting points.
quests.explanation: One walk on one day cannot hold three benefits. The other options are wide enough to cover several points, though one is more general than the others.

quests.instruction: Choose the most specific support.
quests.prompt: Claim: The canteen should offer cheaper meals.
options: It costs too much money for what you actually get.
A lunch costs £4.50, so one week of lunches costs £22.50 per student.
Many people think that the food is quite expensive.
Prices in the canteen are high for lots of students.
quests.hint: Specific support gives numbers, names or details you could check.
quests.explanation: This answer gives real amounts. The alternatives give impressions such as 'high' and 'too much' without any detail.

quests.instruction: Choose the most specific support.
quests.prompt: Claim: Our team should use a shared task board.
options: Last month, two of us worked on the same report for a whole afternoon.
It can waste a lot of time in some cases.
Things sometimes get a bit confusing when we work together.
Teams have problems from time to time in every workplace.
quests.hint: Which sentence describes a particular event?
quests.explanation: The correct answer describes one real situation. The alternatives are general statements that any team could say.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO most specific pieces of support.
quests.prompt: Claim: The gym should open earlier.
options: The 7 a.m. spin class has a waiting list of fifteen members.
Most shift workers finish at 6 a.m., but the gym opens at 8.
An earlier opening time could be helpful for a lot of members.
Many people like to exercise at different times of the day.
quests.hint: Look for details that could be counted or checked.
quests.explanation: Working hours and a waiting list give concrete evidence. The other statements are general and could be said about any gym.

quests.instruction: Put the sentences in order: topic sentence, reason, example, closing sentence.
quests.prompt: Arrange the sentences of this paragraph about lunchtime walks.
options: After a fifteen-minute walk, I finish reports faster than after eating at my desk.
A short walk at lunchtime can improve the whole working afternoon.
Even a brief walk is a small habit with a large effect.
Fresh air and movement help people feel more alert.
quests.hint: The topic sentence introduces the whole idea, and the closing sentence looks back at it.
quests.explanation: The paragraph opens with the main idea, explains why, gives a personal example and ends by summing up.

quests.instruction: Order these sentences into a paragraph.
quests.prompt: Arrange the sentences about exam preparation.
options: My mock maths test revealed that I kept losing marks on fractions.
They show students which topics they still find difficult.
Practice tests are a smart way to prepare for exams.
Testing yourself early leaves time to fix weak spots.
quests.hint: Start with the sentence that introduces the practice test idea as a whole.
quests.explanation: The claim comes first, the reason second, the example third and the closing benefit last.

quests.instruction: Order the sentences. Watch for the phrase that introduces the example.
quests.prompt: Arrange the sentences about what volunteers learn.
options: Volunteers learn to manage time, talk to strangers and solve problems.
Volunteering can teach practical skills.
For instance, my sister now runs a food bank desk and trains new helpers.
These are skills that many employers value.
quests.hint: Phrases such as 'for instance' come after the idea they illustrate.
quests.explanation: The idea comes first, followed by an explanation, then 'for instance' introduces the example, and the last sentence shows why it matters.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that should be removed to keep the paragraph unified.
quests.prompt: 'Team sports teach cooperation. Players learn to share the ball and to trust each other. Football boots come in several different styles. Working towards a goal together builds respect.'
options: Football boots come in several different styles.
Working towards a goal together builds respect.
Team sports teach cooperation.
Players learn to share the ball and to trust each other.
quests.hint: A paragraph is unified when every sentence supports the same main idea.
quests.explanation: The boots sentence has no connection to cooperation. Every other sentence supports the topic sentence.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence to delete from this part of a work email.
quests.prompt: 'Staff would benefit from a short first-aid course. Accidents can happen in any workplace. The course takes only half a day. Several colleagues have also asked for a yoga class.'
options: Staff would benefit from a short first-aid course.
Accidents can happen in any workplace.
Several colleagues have also asked for a yoga class.
The course takes only half a day.
quests.hint: One sentence opens a second, separate request.
quests.explanation: The yoga class is a different suggestion, which weakens the focus on first aid. The rest of the paragraph stays on the course.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO sentences that should be removed.
quests.prompt: 'Our street should get a speed bump. Cars often drive too fast past the playground. A speed bump would slow drivers near the children. The playground was built in 1998. I also think the street needs more trees.'
options: Cars often drive too fast past the playground.
A speed bump would slow drivers near the children.
I also think the street needs more trees.
The playground was built in 1998.
quests.hint: Ask which sentences help prove the need for a speed bump.
quests.explanation: The playground's age and the trees don't support the speed bump argument. The other two explain the danger and the solution.

quests.instruction: Choose the best concluding sentence for the paragraph.
quests.prompt: The paragraph gives reasons why learning an instrument builds patience, improves memory and gives students confidence.
options: For these reasons, learning an instrument is worth the effort.
I bought my violin at a shop last year.
Some instruments are more expensive than others.
Choir is another good option for young singers.
quests.hint: A conclusion should return to the main claim of the paragraph.
quests.explanation: The best sentence sums up the paragraph's claim. The remaining options introduce new details that were not part of the argument.

quests.instruction: Choose the best closing sentence.
quests.prompt: The paragraph argues that shorter Fridays would let staff finish tasks and start the weekend rested.
options: Friday is the fifth day of the normal working week.
Shorter Fridays would leave staff more rested and productive.
There are many different opinions about working hours.
Our company should also change its lunch menu.
quests.hint: The closing sentence should repeat the idea in a fresh way, without adding a new topic.
quests.explanation: The correct sentence restates the benefit. The alternatives are a fact, a vague remark, or a new unrelated suggestion.

quests.instruction: Choose the strongest conclusion.
quests.prompt: The paragraph argues that shoppers should use local shops because money stays in town and shopkeepers know their customers.
options: In conclusion, this paragraph has been about local shops.
Shopping is something that many people do every week.
Some local shops are open on Sunday afternoons.
Shopping locally keeps money in town and builds friendlier streets.
quests.hint: Avoid conclusions that only describe the paragraph itself or add loose facts.
quests.explanation: The correct sentence gathers both reasons. 'In conclusion, this paragraph...' talks about the writing rather than the argument.

quests.instruction: Choose the example that fits BOTH the claim and the reason.
quests.prompt: Claim: Students should get a break between exams. Reason: Tired students make more mistakes.
options: Exam papers are usually collected in the school hall by invigilators, who then take them to the office.
In my Friday double exam, I made careless errors in the second paper because I had no rest.
In my Friday double exam, the second paper had more questions than the first one, and it was longer.
Exam timetables are published a month before the first paper, so students can plan their revision.
quests.hint: The example must show tiredness leading to errors.
quests.explanation: Careless errors after no rest match the reason and the claim. The other options are about exam logistics or paper length.

quests.instruction: Choose the example that supports the reason and the claim.
quests.prompt: Claim: Restaurants should show calories on menus. Reason: People choose better when they can compare.
options: When my cousin saw calories beside two burgers, she chose the smaller one.
Many restaurants have menus with photographs on every page.
Some diners order the same dish every time they visit.
Calories are units that measure the energy in food.
quests.hint: Look for someone comparing and then choosing.
quests.explanation: The cousin compared two options and chose differently because of the information. The others describe menus or habits without showing the effect.

quests.instruction: Choose the example that best fits.
quests.prompt: Claim: Companies should train staff to give clear feedback. Reason: Unclear feedback wastes time.
options: Feedback is often given in meetings, by email or in short chats, depending on what suits the manager.
My manager once said my report was 'off', so I rewrote it twice before learning she only wanted a shorter summary.
My manager once praised my report in front of the whole team, and I felt proud for the rest of that week.
Some companies hold feedback training sessions on the first Friday of each month for all new managers.
quests.hint: The example must show time being lost because of unclear comments.
quests.explanation: Rewriting twice because of a vague comment shows wasted time. The alternatives show praise, types of feedback or training schedules.

quests.instruction: Choose the revision that turns the vague idea into a clear claim.
quests.prompt: Original: 'School uniforms are kind of good and kind of bad.'
options: School uniforms have many different aspects to consider.
Uniforms are worn by students in many different countries.
People think about school uniforms in different ways.
School uniforms should be optional so that families can choose.
quests.hint: A clear claim takes a position that the writer can support.
quests.explanation: 'Should be optional' states a position with a purpose. The other versions describe the topic without deciding anything.

quests.instruction: Which sentence is the clearest version?
quests.prompt: Original: 'Social media is complicated.'
options: Social media is a big topic that people discuss these days.
There are many social media apps that people can use.
Teenagers should limit social media use in the evening to protect their sleep.
Social media has many different kinds of effects on people.
quests.hint: A revision should say who, what and what should be done.
quests.explanation: This version names a group, an action and a purpose. The alternatives remain general descriptions.

quests.instruction: Choose the best revision of the vague comment.
quests.prompt: Original: 'The new system is okay, I guess.'
options: Some people like the new system and some do not.
The new system exists and many people are using it now.
The new system is a system that people use for booking.
The new booking system saves time but needs clearer instructions.
quests.hint: A useful opinion tells the reader what is good and what needs to change.
quests.explanation: The best version gives a judgement and a specific improvement. The others only describe or report other people's views.

quests.instruction: Choose the strongest topic sentence for this paragraph.
quests.prompt: Details: a tidy desk means fewer lost papers; it lets you see the day's tasks at a glance; many people say it lowers their stress.
options: Offices should be quiet places for everyone.
Keeping a tidy desk makes work easier.
Desks in offices are usually made of wood.
Every worker has a favourite kind of pen.
quests.hint: The sentence should cover the details, not just one word from them.
quests.explanation: The best sentence covers lost papers, planning and stress. The remaining options don't connect to the details.

quests.instruction: Put the sentences in the best order.
quests.prompt: Arrange the sentences into a paragraph.
options: Swaps save money and keep good clothes in use.
Clothing swap events are a smart alternative to buying new clothes.
At last spring's swap, I left with three shirts and a coat for free.
People can refresh their wardrobes without spending any money.
quests.hint: Look for the sentence that could introduce the whole paragraph.
quests.explanation: The paragraph moves from the main idea to a reason, an example and a closing benefit.

quests.instruction: Choose the strongest paragraph.
quests.prompt: Four students wrote about switching off phones in cinemas. Which paragraph has a claim, specific support and a focused ending?
options: Phones should be switched off in cinemas. This can be a problem sometimes for people. Some people do things that others do not like. It would be better for everyone in the end.
Bright screens distract people sitting nearby. Last month, a glowing screen in front of me made me miss a key scene. Silence protects everyone's evening. Cinemas should sell more comfortable seats.
Phones should be switched off in cinemas. Bright screens distract people sitting nearby. Last month, a glowing screen in front of me made me miss a key scene. Silence protects everyone's evening.
Phones should be switched off in cinemas. Bright screens distract people sitting nearby. Popcorn is also very expensive at most cinemas. Silence protects everyone's evening.
quests.hint: Check for a clear claim, relevant support and unity.
quests.explanation: The first paragraph has all parts and every sentence is on topic. The others are vague, contain a sentence about popcorn, or lack a topic sentence and end with an unrelated idea.
